title: Client rejected the server certificate — 'unknown CA' TLS alert
plain_english: The TLS handshake was aborted by the client device: it sent a fatal 'unknown CA' alert, meaning it does not trust the certificate your RADIUS server presented. This is a client-side trust decision — the handshake died before the server ever saw the user's credentials.

causes.cause: The client device doesn't have — or doesn't trust — the CA that signed your RADIUS server certificate. Typical right after switching from a self-signed certificate or migrating to a new CA.
causes.next_check: On one failing device, confirm the CA certificate is installed and that the Wi-Fi/802.1X profile actually references it (Windows and Android profiles pin specific CAs; installing the cert alone is not enough).

causes.cause: The server sends an incomplete chain — the intermediate CA is missing, so clients cannot build a path to a trusted root.
causes.next_check: Verify certificate_file in mods-available/eap contains the server cert followed by every intermediate; test the presented chain with eapol_test or openssl s_client.

causes.cause: Clients validate the server name and the certificate's CN/SAN changed at renewal.
causes.next_check: Compare the certificate's subjectAltName with the server name configured in the clients' Wi-Fi profile.
